title: Cotangent determinant normalization of the canonical adjunction line
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $p:W\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]), with every nonempty geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] pure of dimension $d\geq0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Suppose $W$ is covered by factorizations $U\xrightarrow{i}P\to S$ with $P$ open in $\mathbf A^n_S$ and $i$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal $I$ is locally generated by a regular sequence of length $c=n-d$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Let $K=K_{W/S}$ and its canonical comparison maps from $K_i=(\bigwedge^c I/I^2)^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^n i^*\Omega^1_{P/S}$ be the adjunction line and comparisons of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction]. Let $L=L_{W/S}$ and $\lambda_i:E_i=[I/I^2\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}i^*\Omega^1_{P/S}]\xrightarrow{\sim}L|_U$ be the intrinsic cotangent complex and its conormal model comparisons of [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation]. Exterior powers, duals and pullbacks in these formulas use the conventions of the two cited nodes. There is a canonical isomorphism $\theta:K\xrightarrow{\sim}\det L$ for the determinant functor of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant], with the following normalization: for every presentation $i$, the composite $K_i\to K|_U\xrightarrow{\theta}\det L|_U$ is the local exterior-model identification $K_i=D(E_i)$ followed by $\det(\lambda_i)$. Consequently, on every overlap the specified adjunction transition $K_i\to K_j$ is exactly $\det(\lambda_j^{-1}\lambda_i)$ under the exterior-model identifications. This normalization is compatible with arbitrary base changes $S'\to S$: the comparison $g^*K\simeq K_{W\times_SS'/S'}$ specified in the adjunction lemma becomes, under $\theta$, the composite $g^*\det L\simeq\det(Lg^*L)\simeq\det L_{W\times_SS'/S'}$ of the determinant pullback comparison and the intrinsic cotangent base-change comparison. The assertion after base change is about the pulled-back local models and applies even if $S'$ is not Noetherian. No morphism from differentials to $K$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0B6V (lemma-lci-shriek), local Koszul adjunction line, together with perfect.tex Tags 0FJX (lemma-determinant-two-term-complexes) and 0FJY (remark-functorial-det). Agent-formulated identification of the normalized comparisons; the tags do not state this full comparison verbatim.

proof.text: Write $a_i:K_i\to K|_U$ for the specified adjunction comparisons. A regular sequence is Koszul-regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular], so the conormal model theorem [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] applies to every presentation in the statement. Apply [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] to $\lambda_i:E_i\simeq L|_U$ and set $\alpha_i=\det(\lambda_i):K_i=D(E_i)\to(\det L)|_U$. The issue is to compare the specified $a_j^{-1}a_i$ with $\alpha_j^{-1}\alpha_i$; an abstract isomorphism between the underlying lines would not suffice.

Work on affine subcharts over an affine open of $S$. These source charts are separated over that base, so [lem-trf-relative-duality-polynomial-chart] applies: flatness and local finite presentation are inherited from $p$, and the base is locally Noetherian. Its statement supplies the normalized comparisons of the local dualizing models under polynomial refinement. By [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction], the adjunction line shifted by $d=n-c$ is precisely this relative dualizing object, locally with its specified Koszul Ext identification. Thus the comparisons defining $a_i$ are obtained by restricting those polynomial-model comparisons to their single nonzero cohomology module. This uses the dualizing and Ext clauses of the cited statements, not the construction of $K$ inside a cited proof. It remains to calculate their effect on the displayed generators.

On a fixed ambient chart choose equations $f_1,\ldots,f_c$. Their classes are a basis of $C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free]. The ideal-independent top Ext identification of [lem-sc-koszul-regular-sequence-dual-complex] is the dual of their top conormal wedge. Replacing that basis by $\bar f'=M\bar f$ multiplies its dual top wedge by $\det(M)^{-1}$, exactly as in $D(E)=(\bigwedge^c C)^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^n V$; a change of basis in $V$ acts by its top wedge on both sides. Consequently the Koszul and determinant identifications agree under changing regular equations or differential frames. They agree under restriction as well: the Koszul comparison commutes with localization by its cited statement, and the determinant comparison commutes with restriction by [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant]. No invertibility of the coefficient matrix over the ambient ring is needed: its reduction on $C$ is a basis change over the quotient.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ (lemma-regular-immersion-ext), top Koszul cohomology; perfect.tex Tag 0FJX, exterior-model formula.

proof.text:
For a one-coordinate refinement put $Q=A[t]$, $h=t-a$, and let $B=A/I$ be the source ring. The new conormal module is $Bh\oplus C$ and the new differential module is $B\,dh\oplus V$, where $dh=dt-da$; substitution $t=a$ projects their complex onto $E=[C\to V]$, with kernel $[Bh\xrightarrow{1}B\,dh]$. Naturality in [lem-trf-lci-naive-cotangent-model] identifies this projection in the derived category with the intrinsic model comparison $\lambda_i^{-1}\lambda_{\mathrm{new}}$. The determinant is the kernel-first map of [lem-trf-affine-two-term-determinant] and [lem-trf-surjective-two-term-determinant-calculus]. It sends
$$ (\bar h\wedge\bar f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar f_c)^\vee\otimes(dh\wedge v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_n)\quad\hbox{to}\quad(\bar f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar f_c)^\vee\otimes(v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_n). $$
Indeed the kernel differential sends $\bar h$ to $dh$, so its determinant has value $1$. The polynomial dualizing comparison of [lem-trf-relative-duality-polynomial-chart] contracts exactly $\bar h^\vee\otimes dh$ to $1$ in this order, giving the same formula. There is no implicit exchange of ordered factors: writing $h$ last instead multiplies this displayed generator by $(-1)^{c+n}$ on both sides of the comparison. Iteration uses the same successive kernel-first contractions, and the cited dualizing comparison includes the cohomological tensor signs. Thus determinant and adjunction agree for every iterated polynomial refinement.

source.place: Tag 0BZJ (lemma-well-defined), one-variable effective-Cartier refinement and Tag 0BZI top-differential normalization; more-algebra.tex Tag 0FJM, kernel-first determinant construction.

proof.text:
Locally two polynomial presentations have a common combined-coordinate refinement. Explicitly, for polynomial surjections $R[x]\twoheadrightarrow B$ and $R[y]\twoheadrightarrow B$, lift each image of $y_j$ to $a_j(x)$. Then the combined kernel is generated by the first kernel and $y_j-a_j(x)$: substitution reduces any polynomial to one in $x$, and a polynomial in the kernel then reduces to the first kernel. These added equations are successive monic coordinate equations, so their conormal complexes are precisely the successive refinements just calculated. Reversing $x,y$ gives the other comparison. For ambient opens, restrict around the point to principal pieces and invert the denominators; their images in $B$ are units, so the same substitutions extend after localization. These are the polynomial refinements in [lem-trf-relative-duality-polynomial-chart]. That node gives their composition law; [lem-trf-lci-naive-cotangent-model] identifies their complex maps with the intrinsic comparisons; [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] gives the determinant composition law. Steps 3 and 4 therefore imply, on an open cover of every overlap,
$$a_j^{-1}a_i=\det(\lambda_j^{-1}\lambda_i)=\alpha_j^{-1}\alpha_i.$$
The equality holds on the whole overlap because two sheaf maps agreeing on an open cover agree on every section by the sheaf uniqueness axiom. No affine-intersection hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 0BZJ (lemma-well-defined), combined polynomial presentation diagram; perfect.tex Tag 0FJX, composition of determinant maps.

proof.text: Define on each chart $\theta_i=\alpha_i a_i^{-1}:K|_U\to(\det L)|_U$. The equality in Step 5 gives $\theta_i=\theta_j$ on overlaps. For a section $s$ of $K$ on an open $T$, glue the sections $\theta_i(s|_{T\cap U_i})$ using the sheaf axiom of $\det L$; their agreement gives a unique section, and uniqueness proves linearity and commutation with restrictions. Applying the same construction to $\theta_i^{-1}$ gives its inverse. This constructs a unique global isomorphism $\theta$ with $\theta a_i=\det(\lambda_i)$ for every chart. The construction is forced by these equations, so it is independent of the cover and has precisely the stated normalization.

source.place: Tag 0FJX, sheaf gluing of the local determinant maps; explicit application of the sheaf axiom.

proof.text: For $S'\to S$ use affine base rings $R\to R'$. The pulled-back presentations are again conormal models. Shrink the ambient chart to a principal affine piece $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]_h$ of $P$ on which $I$ is generated by a regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ in $A$, so $B=A/(f)$. The polynomial ring is $R$-free on monomials, hence $R$-flat, so $A$ is $R$-flat by [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness]; by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-polynomial-quotient], $A\cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_n,z]/(hz-1)$ is finitely presented over $R$. Put $A'=A\otimes_RR'$ and $f'_j=f_j\otimes1$, so $A'/(f')=B\otimes_RR'$ and $A'$ is the corresponding principal piece of $\mathbf A^n_{S'}$. Here $B$ is $R$-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. By [lem-pur-relative-regular-equations-base-change] the $f'_j/1$ form a regular sequence in $A'_{\mathfrak q'}$ for every prime $\mathfrak q'$ containing all $f'_j$, hence a Koszul-regular one there by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular]. At a prime not containing some $f'_j$, that $f'_j$ is a unit of $A'_{\mathfrak q'}$; multiplication by $f'_j$ on the Koszul complex is null-homotopic (contraction with the $j$th basis vector), so its homology vanishes. Localization is exact and commutes with forming the Koszul complex, and a module whose localizations at all primes vanish is zero; hence $f'_1,\ldots,f'_c$ is Koszul-regular in $A'$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. So [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] gives the conormal model comparison $\lambda'_i$ of the pulled-back presentation, and by [lem-sc-koszul-conormal-basis] the classes $\bar f'_j$ form a basis of $C'=I'/I'^2$; the natural map $g^*C\to C'$ sends the basis $\bar f_j$ to it and is an isomorphism, while coordinate differentials identify $g^*V$ with $V'$. Thus $g^*E_i\simeq E'_i$ termwise and $g^*D(E_i)\simeq D(E'_i)$.

source.place: Section 062D (section-koszul-regular), Tag 062F (lemma-regular-koszul-regular); the non-flat base change is the agent argument already used in step 7 of lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction.

proof.text:
For $S'\to S$ use affine base rings $R\to R'$ and an affine source ring $B$ over $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], $B$ is $R$-flat. Tensor a flat resolution of $R'$ over $R$ with $B$: flatness preserves exactness, so its only cohomology is $B\otimes_RR'$ in degree zero. Hence the square is Tor-independent, and by the previous step the pulled-back presentations are conormal models with $g^*E_i\simeq E'_i$. The natural comparison $\beta:Lg^*L\simeq L_{W'/S'}$ of [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] is an isomorphism and respects the conormal models. The arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction] supplies the pulled-back adjunction presentations and their line comparisons, even for non-Noetherian $S'$. In particular we are not applying a Noetherian relative-duality existence theorem over $S'$. The determinant pullback comparison of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] now gives
$$b_D:g^*\det L\xrightarrow{\sim}\det(Lg^*L)\xrightarrow{\det(\beta)}\det L_{W'/S'}.$$
All hypotheses of the cotangent and adjunction base-change clauses are thus in force.

source.place: Tag 08QQ (lemma-tensor-product-tor-independent); perfect.tex Tag 0FJY (remark-functorial-det); duality.tex, arbitrary-base-change adjunction construction.

proof.text: Let $b_K:g^*K\to K'$ be the specified adjunction base-change map. On each pulled-back presentation it is extension of the conormal/top-differential formula, by the arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction]. For finite locally free modules the pullback maps on exterior powers and duals send a basis wedge to the corresponding pulled-back basis wedge and its dual to that dual. Thus $g^*D(E_i)\to D(E'_i)$ sends $1\otimes(\bar f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar f_c)^\vee\otimes(v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_n)$ to the identical primed expression. By naturality of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] and the conormal-model compatibility of [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation], this is also the restriction of $b_D$ under $\alpha_i,\alpha'_i$. The generator-change and contraction formulas in Steps 3 and 4 are identities of finite wedges and evaluation over any ring, so they still compare the primed presentation transitions without a Noetherian hypothesis. The sheaf gluing of Step 6 defines $\theta'$ there. On these generators the two maps $\theta' b_K$ and $b_D g^*\theta$ agree, hence they agree on every chart and globally. Identity and successive base changes give the same pure-wedge formulas; alternatively their equality follows from the coherent cotangent and determinant comparisons in the cited statements. This proves all the required base-change normalization, including the assertion over arbitrary $S'$.
